examples.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
examples.problem: List the elements of the set $A=\{k \in \mathbb{Z}: |k-1| \leq 4 \}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality $|k-1| \leq 4.$ So, we first need to solve for $k{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|k-1|\le 4 \\ -4\le k-1\le 4 \\ -3\le k\le 5\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the above inequality are $-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4,5.$ 

Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A = \{0,\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,4,5 \}.
$$

feedback.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:3{x}^{2}+27=0}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation $3{x}^{2}+27=0.$ 

So, we first need to solve our equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+27 & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2} & =-27 \\ {x}^{2} & =-9 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{-9} \\ x & =\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

However, since $x\in R$ and $\pm 3\text{i}\notin R,$ we conclude that the set $A$ contains no elements. Hence, $A=∅.$
